doc.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002

title: Job with the union in 1965 and long-term gigs with Alley, Scobey, Hines, Baranco
summary: As clubs folded he took a union job and summarizes his long engagements from Vernon Alley to Baranco.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: why I went to work for the union, in 1965. So I got a job with the union and so at least I could pay my rent and everything. So then I could afford to be a casual musician. So I would get casual work on the weekends, then I got most of my jobs, I was lucky, they were long term jobs. With Vernon Alley — I worked with Vernon Alley. He was the house band leader for the Black Hawk. And I worked with Vernon because we had been in the Navy together. I worked with him I guess maybe three or four years. Then when they started cutting back I got with Fatha Hines — well Scobey. I went with Scobey for a year and got the Dixieland experience. And then when Fatha Hines came here, the guy at the Club Hangover hired me to replace the drummer. I guess Hines was unhappy with the drummer. So that association lasted seven and a half years. So then after that then that was ’63, ’64 I worked with Slim Jenkins, I worked down at the Mars Club in San Jose. And then in early ’64 Wilbert Baranco hired me to work two nights a week at the Claremont Hotel. He was doing five nights a week and he was up there — I was up there seven years with him.
That’s interesting because he’s the first fella you recorded with, isn’t he?
